reviewers.summary: Source-mode handling covers the named mode and Case B scenarios, but the serial comparison can treat an unrelated component as conflicting evidence. The named tests are included in the repository’s dotnet test AirlineDemo.sln command.

findingList.message: Compare the claim only with the relevant technical record. A serial mismatch on an unrelated component can incorrectly route a supported finding to review.

evidence.codePathTraced: Assess collects every technical pin with a serial number, then treats any serial that differs from the claim as a conflict.
evidence.failureScenario: A claim cites an engine serial that matches its engine record, while the same case has another technical component record with a different serial. The unrelated record makes Any return true, so the assessment is routed to Review with reason source_conflict despite matching evidence for the claimed component.

reviewers.summary: The mode outcome and Case B tests cover their stated behaviors. The concurrent basis-write invariant in the third acceptance criterion is not exercised by its named test.

findingList.message: The race portion of SourceFailuresNeverCreateRequestsAcceptancesOrRefreshBasis does not test a concurrent basis write: it injects the revision change in CreateWorkItem while unavailable mode skips RefreshSourceBasis. Add a race case that exercises the basis commit path and asserts the prior basis history remains unchanged.

evidence.codePathTraced: The race scenario uses unavailable mode, so AssessmentExecutionService skips GatherSourceBasis and RefreshSourceBasis. RacingStore introduces the revision change in CreateWorkItem instead of at a basis commit.
evidence.failureScenario: If basis refresh used an incorrect or non-atomic expected-revision commit, this test would not exercise that path; the basis write is skipped, and the injected conflict occurs during work-item creation. The test therefore does not verify the acceptance criterion’s concurrent basis-write invariant.

reviewers.summary: No security vulnerabilities found in the changed code. Source reads remain behind the existing session, case-scope, role, and budget checks.
